answer: Echo-island inference audit: each fake must burn ~1 GPU-hour of its own reasoning per epoch, so 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 GPU-hours. A verifier sends every key a per-key seeded ridge of 20 chained puzzles; replies are scored and their error patterns compared. Keys whose mistakes echo each other (same wrong steps, latency within 50 ms) are merged into one island sharing a single reward weight. A farm can't reuse one run because seeds differ per key, and one model behind many keys leaves the same error echo. Limit: distinct models evade it, but each adds real cost.
